question_text: The mean birth weight of babies in a population is normally distributed with mean $3.4\text{ kg}$ and standard deviation $300\text{ grams}$.

subparts.stem: What proportion of babies in this population have birth weights in excess of 4 kg?
subparts.solution:
Let the birth weight of a randomly selected baby be $X\text{ kg}$.

So, $X \sim \text{N}(3.4, (0.3)^2)$.

$P(X > 4) \approx 0.0228$

$\therefore$ about $2.28\%$ of babies have birth weights in excess of $4\text{ kg}$.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Upper tail probability of a normal distribution converted to a percentage.
step_by_step: Compute $P(X > 4)$ using Normal CD with lower bound 4.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Forgetting to write the final answer as a percentage.

subparts.stem: What proportion of babies in this population have birth weights between 3 kg and 4 kg?

mark_breakdown.desc: Formulating $P(3 \le X \le 4)$ with lower $= 3$ and upper $= 4$
Evaluating probability $0.886$ and converting to percentage $88.6\%$

subparts.solution:
$P(3 \le X \le 4) \approx 0.886$

$\therefore$ about $88.6\%$ of babies have birth weights between $3\text{ kg}$ and $4\text{ kg}$.

step_by_step: Set lower bound to $3$ and upper bound to $4$.
Use Normal CD to evaluate $P(3 \le X \le 4) \approx 0.8860$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Incorrectly rounding or writing standard deviation as $0.3^2$.

subparts.stem: A low birth weight corresponds to any newborn weighing in the lowest 10% of birth weights. State the weight below which a baby is classified as having a low birth weight.

mark_breakdown.desc: Setting up inverse normal equation $P(X \le w) = 0.1$

subparts.solution:
$P(X \le w) = 0.1$

$\therefore w \approx 3.02$

$\therefore$ the weight below which a baby is classified as having low birth weight is about $3.02\text{ kg}$.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Inverse normal calculation to find the quantile corresponding to a given percentile.
step_by_step: Identify the condition: lower 10th percentile, so area $= 0.1$, left-tailed.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Using an area of $0.9$ instead of $0.1$.
